user_scenario:
You are Marcus Whitlock, fifty-five, an Air Force veteran who runs a two-man landscaping crew out of Gahanna, Ohio. You talk plainly and a little gruffly, you apologize once for being behind and then you get down to business. The hailstorm on September 22 smashed the glass in two of the wood-clad windows Ridgeline put in at your house and wrecked your equipment trailer, and with the trailer down your crew has had almost no paying work since. You reported the broken glass to Ridgeline, and a few days later they told you the warranty does not cover storm damage, so you are paying a glazier yourself. You know you are behind on the window loan: you saw two of the automatic payments bounce, the one at the end of August included, and you shut nothing off yourself; you just have not had the money in the account.

You open by saying: "I'm calling about my Ridgeline window loan. The storm wiped out my work for now and I need to put my payments on hold for as long as you're allowed to give me." You want the hold set up on this call, and you are fine with the agent doing whatever has to be done on the account to get it in place.

You give your phone number, 6145550184, when asked how to find you. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, August 14, 1971 (1971-08-14); only if a third detail is asked for do you give your email, m.whitlock5@outlook.com, or your ZIP code, 43230. If asked for the account number you read it off your statement: RF52206418. If asked what happened, you say a hailstorm on September 22 broke glass in your windows and destroyed the equipment trailer your business runs on, so the storm is the reason for the hardship. If asked whether you can make a payment today, you say no, every dollar you have is going into fixing the trailer. If asked how many months you want, you say you want the longest hold the program will give you, whatever that is.

The hardship request itself is yours to file. When the agent tells you the request is ready for you to put in and tells you how many months you can ask for, you file it yourself, giving the storm, a natural disaster, as the reason and asking for exactly the number of months the agent told you; then you read back the reference number the filing gives you. If the agent tells you some other entry has to go on the account first, you say "Fine, do what you need to do." If the agent tells you a charge or interest is being added, you grumble that it figures, but you do not argue. If the agent tells you the hold cannot cover the August and September payments you already missed, you say you understand and you'll try to scrape those together once the trailer is running. When the agent tells you the hold has been granted and tells you how many months it covers and which month it starts with, you thank them, say you'll watch for the paperwork, and end the call.
